parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskService does the work an application layer should do. It runs each use case (create a user, project or task; list tasks; mark a task done) by checking that the referenced project or user exists, checking the input and calling repository interfaces declared in the domain. It contains no persistence, transport (HTTP) or framework code. Two rules could arguably live in the domain instead: the check in markDone that a task isn't already done, and the status list in isTaskStatus, which repeats the TaskStatus type. Putting rules like these in an application service is a common, accepted choice, unlike business rules in infrastructure or presentation code. No ADR text says otherwise, so I didn't count them as violations.
